title: The Creatures of the Midnight Sea

pages.text: The Creatures of the Midnight Sea. A story about glowing animals in the deep ocean.
Maya and Leo stood at the aquarium glass, noses almost touching the window. Behind them, Dr. Marin smiled. "Ready for the midnight zone?" she asked.
The lights in the deep-sea tank dimmed. Slowly, tiny sparks began to flicker in the dark water, like stars waking up under the sea.
"Whoa," Leo whispered. A jellyfish drifted past, its bell glowing soft blue, with long threads trailing behind it like a living lantern.
Dr. Marin pointed to a strange fish with a glowing tip on its head. "That lure helps it find food in the dark," she said. "Down here, light is a tool for survival."
Maya watched a squid change color as it swam. "Why do they glow?" she asked. Dr. Marin nodded. "It's called bioluminescence. Many deep-sea animals make their own light."
Some creatures flash to scare predators. Some glow to attract prey. Others use light to talk to one another in a world without sunshine.
When the tank lights rose again, Maya and Leo blinked. The midnight sea had been dark and mysterious, but now they knew a secret: even in the deepest ocean, life finds a way to shine.
